title: Maize — Disease Management: Downy Mildew, Stalk Rot, Blight
content:
MAJOR DISEASES OF MAIZE:

1. DOWNY MILDEW (Peronosclerospora sorghi):
Symptoms: Chlorotic stripes on leaves, white downy growth on lower surface, stunted plants.
Management: Seed treatment with Metalaxyl 35 SD @ 6g/kg seed. Metalaxyl 8%+Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L spray at 15 DAS. Destroy infected plants.

2. TURCICUM BLIGHT (Northern Leaf Blight — Exserohilum turcicum):
Symptoms: Large cigar-shaped grayish-green lesions on leaves.
Management: Propiconazole 25 EC @ 1 ml/L or Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2g/L spray.

3. STALK ROT (Fusarium + Pythium):
Symptoms: Internal rot of stalk, lodging, premature plant death.
Management: Captan 0.2% stem spray. Avoid water stress at silking. Balanced NPK.
Prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen, maintain K levels.

4. MAIZE LETHAL NECROSIS (MLN — new threat):
Symptoms: Yellowing from leaf tips, necrosis, ear tip bareness, plant death.
Management: No effective chemical. Use MLN-tolerant varieties (H614D, DH02). Control aphids and thrips (vectors). Destroy infected crop residues.

5. SMUT (Ustilago maydis):
Symptoms: Galls on ears, tassels and leaves — white then black.
Management: Use smut-free seed. Captan 3g/kg seed treatment. Remove and destroy galls before sporulation.

GENERAL DISEASE MANAGEMENT:
- Use disease-resistant hybrids.
- Crop rotation with non-graminaceous crops.
- Balanced nutrition — excess N promotes many diseases.
- Good drainage prevents soilborne diseases.
